text:
Sasha: heads-up, eu-west spot pool just flipped a bunch of instances (NVIDIA A10s) — a few streaming requests got cut mid-token. symptoms: partial chunks, client saw EOF. anyone else seeing spikes? :rotating_light:

infra-bot: [alert] 1768001153 - GCE_PREEMPTION events detected on eu-west1-b: count=18 in 3m. avg-remaining-lifetime=27s. recommended-action=drain-graceful-or-requeue

Jaya: I saw that. two long-running chats (>= 120s) lost their streams. logs show preStop ran but we don't currently emit a resumable checkpoint for token streams.

Marco: can we do a best-effort token-bridge? pattern: on preempt-warn -> snapshot last N tokens + KV pointers -> issue ephemeral resume-token to client -> requeue request to scheduler with resume-token metadata. client then reconnects to new pod with resume-token.

Sasha: yes that pattern, but watch latency. if remaining-lifetime < 20s we should prefer immediate requeue to dedicated fallback. requeue adds ~200ms dispatch on average vs dedicated handoff ~600ms but dedicated keeps continuity for long sessions.

Marta: quick config proposal, throwing it here for feedback:
```
requeue_policy:
  enabled: true
  window_s: 25
  max_attempts: 3
  prefer_dedicated_on_retry: true
  resume_token_ttl_s: 90
```

Marco: +1 to TTL 90s. also we need a handshake protocol: resume-token must include KV-checkpoint-id and client-offset. pseudo: `{"token_id":"r-abc123","kv_id":"k-987","offset":384}` and sign it. runtime should validate and perform kv-merge on attach.

Jaya: infra implications: Redis master is in eu-west1; when we requeue across regions you may lose low-latency access. let's limit token-bridge to region-local only or use our cross-region read replica read-path.

Sasha: good call. prefer region-local bridging. fallback: if cross-region then immediately requeue to dedicated in target region or serve with stateless model (short completion) to close the stream gracefully.

oncall: rolling alert note — I'm increasing spot pool buffer by 15% for eu-west for the next 2h to reduce immediate churn. will monitor eviction rate.

Marta: ops question — how do we measure success? suggested SLOs: percentage of streams resumed with resume-token >= 95% and median extra-latency on resume < 350ms.

Marco: for safety, add circuit-breaker on streaming-resume failures. if resume fails > 5% over 5m, disable token-bridge for that pool and fall back to requeue to dedicated.

Sasha: implementation notes for runtime team:
- preempt hook: on WARN -> persist minimal checkpoint to redis (key with short TTL) -> sign and return resume-token to client -> trigger soft-drain (stop accepting new requests, finish inflight if < token-window) -> if inflight cannot finish in remaining-lifetime, call scheduler requeue API with resume-token metadata.
- k8s drain command for manual test: `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120`
- unit test: simulate GCE_PREEMPTION with 15s remain and assert resume-token validity and reattach flow.

Jaya: small code sketch for scheduler requeue payload:
```
{
  "job_id": "j-1234",
  "resume_token": "r-abc123",
  "attempt": 2,
  "prefer_dedicated": true
}
```

Marco: runtime caveat — for mixed-capacity pools we must ensure GPU capability compatibility. resume-token should include model-variant hints so scheduler picks a node with appropriate quantization/compute profile. otherwise we get silent failures.

Sasha: ops-cost tradeoff: enabling token-bridge + region-local replica increases Redis ops and slightly higher tail-latency; but reduces wasted tokens (cost) and user-facing errors. preliminary calc: for eu-west, bridging expected to save ~12% per-token cost on long sessions vs always failing over to dedicated.

Marta: can we do a canary: enable token-bridge on 10% of spot pool and monitor resume-success and extra-latency? if metrics look good flip to 50%, then 100%.

oncall: will run the 10% canary tonight 23:00 UTC. I'll post updates in this thread. tagging @infra-rotation for visibility.

Sasha: thanks — next steps: (1) runtime team to add preempt hook + resume-token path (2) scheduler to accept requeue payload with resume-token (3) ops to enable region-local Redis replica for eu-west canary (4) define metrics dashboard (resume_success_rate, resume_latency_ms, requeue_count).

Marco: plan LGTM. I'll open a small RFC with protocol details and example signed token format.

Jaya: I'll prepare the canary runbook and failure rollback steps (disable token-bridge, increase spot buffer, force dedicated fallback).

infra-bot: [action] created issue INF-4227 for token-bridge RFC.

Sasha: :thumbsup: — keep updates here. if we see new mass preemptions, escalate to paging.
